chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — or from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) — who said:
If a people besiege a city and those inside ask them for security (aman), and they say 'no', but the besieged think they said 'yes', and they descend to them, they would be under protection.

key_terms.آمنين: Amineen — those in a state of aman/protection; the opposite of being at war or under threat
key_terms.الأمان: Aman — a formal guarantee of security granted to non-combatants or enemy soldiers; once given (even inadvertently), it is binding on Muslims
key_terms.ظن: Zann — presumption or reasonable belief; in jurisprudence this can create binding legal consequences when it results in good-faith action

ai.seo_question: In Islamic law, if enemies mistakenly believe they were granted safety and surrender, must Muslims honor it?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes a significant principle in Islamic law of war (fiqh al-jihad): the protection of life (aman) takes precedence over the technical wording of a refusal when a genuine misunderstanding arises. Imam al-Sadiq (or al-Kazim/al-Ridha, peace be upon them) ruled that if the besieged party sincerely believed they had received a guarantee of safety and surrendered in good faith, the Muslim forces are bound to honor that protection. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that good-faith belief (zann) can create binding obligations in matters of life and safety.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Al Hakam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, or from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘If a people are surrounded in a city, so they ask them (Muslim army) for the sercurity, so they say, ‘No’, and they (mistakenly) think that they said yes, and they descend to them, they would be the secured ones’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn al-Hakam from abu ‘Abd Allah, or abu al- Hassan, recipients of divine supreme covenant, who has said the following: “

If a people surrounds a city and the people of the city ask for immunity and they reply negatively to their request but they think it is a positive response and came out of their fortress, such people are entitled to a binding commitment of immunity.”
